problems.title: Write the contract
problems.statement: For "is the tree height-balanced?" (every node's subtree heights differ by at most 1), in O(n).

options: the height, or −1 if the subtree is unbalanced

hints: Returning only a bool forces recomputing heights.
problems.solution: Return the height with −1 as an "unbalanced" sentinel; the parent needs heights to check itself. A bool-only recursion calling height() at each node is O(n²) on a path-like tree.

problems.title: Depth
problems.statement: Tree in level order: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, null, null, 6, null, null, 7].
hints: Draw it: 4 and 5 are children of 2; 6 is under 4, 7 under 5.
problems.solution: Depth 4 (1→2→4→6). The diameter bends at 2: the height of the 4-subtree is 2 and of the 5-subtree is 2, so 2 + 2 = 4 edges (6→4→2→5→7).

problems.title: Max path sum

parts.prompt: Best downward gain returned by the node 20?

problems.solution: gain(20) = 35. Bending at 20: 15 + 20 + 7 = 42, which beats anything through −10 (9 − 10 + 35 = 34). Answer 42.

problems.title: Why clamp?

options: A branch with negative gain is better omitted

parts.prompt: Why must best start at −∞, not 0?
options: All values may be negative and the path must be non-empty

problems.solution: Clamping drops harmful branches. Starting at 0 would wrongly return 0 for [−3].

problems.title: Top-down or bottom-up?

parts.prompt: Count nodes whose value is ≥ every value on the path from the root ("good nodes"):
options: top-down: pass the max so far

parts.prompt: Size of the largest subtree that is a BST:

hints: Does the answer depend on ancestors or on descendants?
problems.solution: Good nodes depend on ancestors, so pass the maximum down. The largest BST subtree depends on descendants, so return a summary tuple.

problems.title: Minimum depth bug
problems.statement: def min_depth(n): return 0 if not n else 1 + min(min_depth(n.left), min_depth(n.right)) on the tree [1, 2] (2 is the left child).

parts.prompt: What does the buggy code return?

hints: The root is not a leaf: it has a child.
problems.solution: The None right child returns 0, so the code says 1. But depth is measured to a leaf, and the only leaf is 2: the answer is 2. When one child is None, recurse only into the other.

problems.title: Recursion depth
problems.statement: A degenerate (path-shaped) tree with 10⁵ nodes, solved recursively in Python.
problems.solution: Python's default limit is 1,000. Raise it (and possibly the thread stack size), or convert to an explicit stack.

problems.title: House robber III
problems.statement: On a tree you may not take both a node and its child. Maximise the sum taken from [3, 4, 5, 1, 3, null, 1].

options: (best if node is taken, best if not taken)

hints: A pair of states per node.
problems.solution: f returns (take, skip). take = val + skip(l) + skip(r); skip = max(l) + max(r). Taking 4 and 5 gives 9, versus 3 + 1 + 3 + 1 = 8.

problems.title: Path sum III
problems.statement: Count downward paths (starting anywhere) whose sum equals k, in O(n).

options: Prefix sums along the root path with a hash map: add on entry, remove on exit

problems.solution: Running DFS from every node is O(n·h). The prefix-sum map gives O(n). Undo the map entry on the way back up, so sibling branches don't see each other's prefixes.
